cim: Principal: Juvenile used AI to make nude images of Chatham Co. charter school students & staff
cim_eredeti: Principal: Juvenile used AI to make nude images of Chatham Co. charter school students & staff
szoveg_eredeti:
A juvenile is accused of using artificial intelligence to create nude images and videos of students and staff at a Chatham County charter school, the school's principal wrote in a letter sent to parents.

In the letter, a copy of which was obtained by WRAL News, Woods Charter School Principal Cotton Bryan said Chatham County deputies told school administrators that a person used artificial intelligence to transform normal photos of dozens of students and staff into nude photos and videos.

"Some of this AI-altered material was then traded on the internet," Bryan wrote.

According to Bryan, the person had pictures or videos of 47 current and former students and 14 current and former faculty members. Bryan added that there are other victims outside of the school's community, but they have not received any additional details related to the other victims.

It is unclear which AI program the minor used.

"We are cooperating fully with the Sheriff’s Office. We have also reached out to outside expertise, specifically the Orange County Rape Crisis Center and Second Bloom of Chatham, two groups who have experience supporting students, adults, and families through traumatic experiences such as this. They will be on hand at Woods this week and in the weeks ahead to assist in our support,” Bryan wrote.

Bryan said Chatham County deputies told him the person they believe is responsible is a juvenile and that the school understood they would be charged and taken into custody soon.

When asked about the case, the Chatham County Sheriff's Office declined to share specifics, stating only that it was conducting a criminal investigation involving the juvenile.

“We are 100% committed to walking alongside all of our families as they navigate the path ahead. The school has faced hardship before, and I know that this community has the heart and the skill to respond with deep care,” Bryan said.

In 2024, state lawmakers updated North Carolina's sexual extortion laws to include language prohibiting the use of "artificial intelligence" as a means of producing pornographic material.

It is not the first case this year involving a juvenile accused of using AI to make nude images of teens. In July, Wake County authorities charged a boy with 10 counts of sexual exploitation of a minor, saying he used AI to create sexually explicit images of underage girls.

In that case, parents who spoke with WRAL on the condition of anonymity expressed concern that content that would be viewed as sexually explicit to the general public is not considered the same in the eyes of the law.
